label: original-phase input token a (positions 0-6)
explanation: Token detector for the letter a as an original-sequence input. Fires on essentially every original-phase step whose input is a at positions 0-6 (dev P=1.00, R=0.996), and almost never at positions 7-8, never on the <DEL> step, and only ~166 tiny activations in the copy phase (even though a is fed back as input there). Never fires on any other token. Magnitude is highest for a at position 2 after a short prefix (e.g. k r a, max 2.28), ~0.83 when a is the first token, and weaker for a repeated a later in the sequence (in_first=0 activations are mostly low-quartile).

issues: All factual claims hold. Test split: precision 1.000, recall 0.995, F1 0.998, mass recall 0.9997, with 0 false positives. The 478 missed steps hold 0.0% of the activation mass. They are tiny activations (0.02-0.05 of max) on a at position 7, plus copy-phase a inputs right after <DEL>. This is a weak tail, not a systematic gap.

Checked against the profile: the feature fires only when the input token is a (in_tok lift 32.9x, 0 activations on any other token). It never fires on <DEL>. The copy phase has only 166 active steps on dev, with ~0 mass. At orig_idx 7 there are 267 activations at rate 0.002, against ~0.033 for positions 0-6. At orig_idx 8 there are none.
The ablation claims reproduce on test. Without orig_idx<7, precision is 0.922. Adding in_first==1 brings recall down to 0.913.

One gap in the magnitude description: mean activation drops steeply after position 2. Mass share divided by active count is about 1.40e-5 at t=2 versus 0.17e-5 at t=6. So a at positions 5-6 fires weakly. The explanation only notes the peak at position 2 and that repeated a's are weaker. This is a missing detail, not an error in the label.
